push_headlines: Oil posted a second weekly loss on surplus worries: Brent settled Friday at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56, weekly moves of -2.52% and -2.50%.
Asia split Friday on the Nvidia CEO exit: the Nikkei +0.53% to 61,142.35, the Hang Seng -1.55% to 23,637.60, the Kospi -0.98%.
Europe notched a third straight record: the STOXX 600 +0.02% to 664.14, capping a +2.4% week, its best since June.
on_notice: Asia reopens first: Hong Kong has fallen three sessions in a row and the Hang Seng Tech index -3% on Friday, so watch whether the AI selloff tied to Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia carries into Monday.
Oil's focus has shifted from shortages to surplus after the IEA flagged a growing glut, but attacks on shipping around the US blockade of Iran remain a supply risk.
Fed hike bets: fed funds futures earlier this month priced roughly an 80% chance of a hike at the December 8-9 meeting, so US data this week can move S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures.

asia.headline: Tokyo rose and Seoul fell on Friday as markets weighed the fallout from Nvidia's leadership change.
asia.detail: The Nikkei 225 +0.53% to 61,142.35, while South Korea's Kospi -0.98% to 5,290.53. Seven of ten Asian benchmarks closed lower; Taiwan's Taiex +1.35% led the gainers. Markets reopen Monday morning local time; this page has Friday's closes.

china.headline: Hong Kong fell for a third straight session; no verified Shanghai close was found.
china.detail: The Hang Seng -1.55% to 23,637.60, down 370.95 points, as the Hang Seng Tech index -3% on AI worries. Searches returned no citable Shanghai Composite close for Friday, so no mainland level is quoted here.

europe.headline: The STOXX 600 closed at a third straight record and its best week since June.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 +0.02% to 664.14, just above Thursday's record of 664.01, for a weekly gain of about 2.4%. The Euro STOXX 50 -0.19% to 6,386.86, a +3.51% week. Insurers and oil majors offset a chip selloff; no confirmed DAX or FTSE 100 close was found.

latam.headline: No Ibovespa close for Friday was found.
latam.detail: The latest verified Ibovespa reading is Wednesday's 172,301.21 (+0.56%). The index has rebounded from 165,528.92 on 3 November, its lowest close since the runoff, while the dollar has held near R$5.50.

mideast.headline: Oil fell for a second straight week as surplus worries outweighed Middle East risk.
mideast.detail: Brent settled Friday at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56, nearly unchanged on the day; for the week Brent -2.52% and WTI -2.50%. Reuters cited lower geopolitical risk from the US-Israeli war against Iran and an IEA report pointing to a larger global surplus, though attacks on shipping continue to pose a supply risk.
